literal: In the second month of the first year of Kaihuang of Sui she left the laity and became a nun, changing her name to Fajing.
idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Kaihuang she left secular life and became a nun, taking the name Fajing.

literal: In the sixth year she died and was buried west of the capital with nun's rites.
idiomatic: In the sixth year she died and was buried west of the capital with the rites of a nun.

literal: The empress's father Sheng, in youth because of the Yuan clan's imperial house, was appointed opening the government.
idiomatic: Her father Sheng, as a young man of the Yuan imperial clan, was appointed commander of the opening-the-government rank.

literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Daxiang, because he was the empress's father he was advanced to supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed Duke of Yi.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Daxiang, as the empress's father, he was promoted to supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

literal: Xuandi's empress Yuchi, named Fanchi, was the granddaughter of Duke of Shu Jiong.
idiomatic: Xuandi's empress Yuchi, named Fanchi, was the granddaughter of the Duke of Shu, Jiong.

literal: She had beautiful looks.
idiomatic: She was renowned for her beauty.

literal: At first she was married to Xi Yanggong Wen, son of Duke of Qi Liang; by the precedent for clan wives she entered court; the emperor forced and favored her.
idiomatic: She had first been married to Wen, son of Duke of Qi Liang, bearing the title Lady of Xi Yang; as a clan wife she entered court on the usual rounds, where the emperor forced himself on her.

literal: When Liang plotted rebellion the emperor executed Wen and pursued the empress into the palace, appointing her Senior Noble Consort.
idiomatic: When Liang plotted rebellion the emperor executed Wen, brought her into the palace, and made her Senior Noble Consort.

literal: In the third month of the second year of Daxiang she was established Heavenly Left Great Empress.
idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Daxiang she was made Heavenly Left Great Empress.

literal: When the emperor died the empress left the laity and became a nun, changing her name to Huadao.
idiomatic: When the emperor died she left secular life and became a nun, taking the name Huadao.

literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui she died.
idiomatic: She died in the fifteenth year of Kaihuang.

literal: Empress Dugu the Literary of Sui, tabooed Jialuo, was a man of Luoyang in Henan, daughter of Grand Marshal and Duke of Wei Xin of Zhou.
idiomatic: Empress Dugu the Literary of Sui, taboo name Jialuo, was from Luoyang in Henan, daughter of Zhou's Grand Marshal and Duke of Wei, Xin.

literal: Xin saw Wendi had an extraordinary countenance and therefore gave him the empress as wife.
idiomatic: Xin saw that Wendi bore an extraordinary countenance and gave him Jialuo as his wife.

literal: She was then fourteen.
idiomatic: She was fourteen at the time.

literal: The emperor and empress were well matched; they swore no children by another.
idiomatic: Emperor and empress were devoted to each other and swore they would have no children by anyone else.

literal: The empress's elder sister was empress to Zhou Mingdi; the eldest daughter was empress to Zhou Xuandi;
idiomatic: Her elder sister became empress to Zhou Mingdi; her eldest daughter became empress to Zhou Xuandi;

literal: the glory of noble kin — none could compare — yet the empress each time kept humble self-restraint.
idiomatic: no family of imperial kin could match their glory — yet the empress always remained humble and restrained.

literal: When Zhou Xuandi died Wendi dwelt in the forbidden quarters and held all government.
idiomatic: When Zhou Xuandi died Wendi held the inner palace and directed all government.

literal: The empress sent Li Yuantong to tell Wendi: "One who rides a beast cannot dismount — exert yourself!
idiomatic: The empress sent Li Yuantong to tell him, "Once you mount the beast you cannot dismount — press on!

literal: " When the emperor received the abdication she was established empress.
idiomatic: " When he took the throne she was made empress.

literal: The Türk once traded with the central states; there was a basket of bright pearls worth eight million.
idiomatic: The Türk once traded with the central states; a basket of luminous pearls was offered at eight million.

literal: Regional commander of Youzhou Yin Shou reported to the empress to buy them.
idiomatic: The regional commander of Youzhou, Yin Shou, asked the empress to purchase them.

literal: The empress said: "Nowadays the barbarians repeatedly raid; soldiers and officers are weary — better to divide the eight million as reward for those with merit.
idiomatic: The empress said, "The frontier tribes raid again and again and the troops are exhausted — better to divide the eight million among those who have earned merit.

literal: " All officials hearing it completely congratulated.
idiomatic: " All the officials, hearing this, offered their congratulations.

literal: Wendi greatly favored and also feared her.
idiomatic: Wendi both doted on her and stood in awe of her.

literal: Whenever the emperor attended court the empress always rode up with him in the imperial carriage to the gate and then stopped.
idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held court the empress rode with him in the imperial carriage as far as the gate, then stopped.

literal: She had palace officers watch the emperor; when governance went astray she at once corrected and remonstrated — much was broadly benefited.
idiomatic: She had palace officers watch him; when his governance went astray she corrected and remonstrated at once — to great benefit.

literal: She waited until the emperor left court and together returned to feast and sleep, looking at each other with pleasure.
idiomatic: She waited until he left court and they returned together to feast and sleep, regarding each other with quiet joy.

literal: The empress early lost both parents and always cherished longing; seeing ministers and grandees who had parents she often extended courtesy to them.
idiomatic: Having lost both parents early she always cherished their memory; when she met ministers who still had parents she often showed them special courtesy.

literal: The authorities memorialized: "In the Zhou Rites, the wives of the hundred officials receive appointment from the queen.
idiomatic: The authorities memorialized, "In the Zhou Rites, the wives of the hundred officials receive appointment from the queen.

literal: The statutes and models are in the past — please follow the ancient system.
idiomatic: The statutes of old are on record — we ask that the ancient system be followed.

literal: " The empress said: "To let women join in government may begin from this — the source cannot be opened.
idiomatic: " The empress said, "To let women share in government may begin with this step — that door must not be opened.

literal: " She did not permit it.
idiomatic: " She refused.

literal: The empress often told the princesses: "The princesses of the Zhou house mostly lacked wifely virtue, were without ritual toward parents-in-law, and estranged kin from flesh — this is not the compliant way; you must warn against it.
idiomatic: She often told the princesses, "The Zhou princesses mostly lacked wifely virtue, failed in ritual toward their husbands' parents, and drove wedges between kin — you must guard against such conduct.

literal: The empress's cousin by marriage Colonel Cui Changren violated the law and should have been beheaded; Wendi because of the empress pardoned him.
idiomatic: Her cousin by marriage, Colonel Cui Changren, committed a capital crime; Wendi would have pardoned him for the empress's sake.

literal: The empress said: "State affairs — how can one look to private ties!
idiomatic: The empress said, "These are affairs of state — how can one favor private ties!

literal: " Changren in the end died for the crime.
idiomatic: " Changren was executed in the end.

literal: Her younger half-brother Tuo by cat-demon witchcraft cursed the empress and for it should have died.
idiomatic: Her younger half-brother Tuo used cat-demon sorcery to curse her and was sentenced to death.

literal: The empress for three days did not eat and pleaded for his life saying: "If Tuo by corrupting government and harming the people — I dare not speak.
idiomatic: For three days she ate nothing and pleaded for his life: "If Tuo harmed the people or corrupted government I would not speak.

literal: Now the crime is for my person — I beg his life.
idiomatic: But his crime was against me alone — I beg for his life.

literal: " Tuo was thereby reduced one degree from death.
idiomatic: " Tuo's sentence was reduced one degree from death.

literal: The empress by nature was elegant and frugal.
idiomatic: By nature she was elegant and frugal.

literal: The emperor often compounded restorative medicine and needed one tael of barbarian powder; within the palace none was used — seeking it, in the end it could not be obtained.
idiomatic: The emperor often prepared restorative medicines needing one tael of barbarian powder; the inner palace kept none in stock and none could be found.

literal: He also wished to bestow on Pillar of State Liu Song's wife a woven collar — within the palace there was also none.
idiomatic: He also wished to give Pillar of State Liu Song's wife a woven collar — the inner palace had none of those either.

literal: The emperor because the empress did not love splendor — at the time Qi's seven-jewel carriage and mirror stand were supremely clever and beautiful — had the carriage destroyed and the mirror stand bestowed on the empress.
idiomatic: Because she disliked luxury, when a supremely fine seven-jewel carriage and mirror stand from Qi arrived, the emperor had the carriage destroyed and gave her only the mirror stand.

literal: The empress elegantly loved reading; penetrating in present and past — whatever she spoke all matched the emperor's intent; within the palace they were called the Two Sages.
idiomatic: She loved books and understood present and past; whatever she advised matched the emperor's mind — within the palace they were called the Two Sages.

literal: Once she dreamed of Zhou's Empress Ashina, who said she suffered bitter punishment and begged merit to be performed.
idiomatic: Once she dreamed of Zhou's Empress Ashina, who said she was suffering bitter punishment and begged that merit be performed for her.

literal: The next day she spoke of it; the emperor for her established a temple to pursue blessing.
idiomatic: The next day she told the emperor, who had a temple built to transfer merit on her behalf.

literal: The empress's elder brother's daughter — her husband died at Bingzhou; the empress's sister-in-law because the girl was pregnant asked that she not go to the funeral.
idiomatic: Her brother's daughter, whose husband had died at Bingzhou, was pregnant; the girl's mother-in-law asked that she not attend the funeral.

literal: The empress said: "A woman's affair is serving the husband — how can she not go!
idiomatic: The empress said, "A woman's duty is to serve her husband — how can she stay away!

literal: If her mother-in-law is present, she should consult her herself.
idiomatic: If her mother-in-law is there, let her ask her directly.

literal: " The mother-in-law did not permit it; the girl then went.
idiomatic: " The mother-in-law refused; the girl went anyway.

literal: The empress was quite benevolent and loving; whenever she heard the Court of Review decide prisoners she never failed to shed tears.
idiomatic: She was deeply benevolent; whenever she heard the Court of Review pass sentence she wept.

literal: Yet her nature was especially jealous; within the rear palace none dared approach the emperor.
idiomatic: Yet she was fiercely jealous; no woman in the rear palace dared approach the emperor.

literal: The granddaughter of Yuchi Jiong had beautiful looks; she was first in the palace; the emperor at Renshou Palace saw and was pleased with her and thereby won favor.
idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong's granddaughter, a great beauty, was already in the palace; the emperor saw her at Renshou Palace, took a liking to her, and favored her.

literal: The empress waited until the emperor attended court and secretly killed her.
idiomatic: The empress waited until he went to court and had her killed in secret.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered, rode alone from the park out, not by the path, and entered a mountain valley more than thirty li.
idiomatic: The emperor was furious, rode alone out of the park by no proper path, and wandered more than thirty li into the hills.

literal: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others pursued and caught up, seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated.
idiomatic: Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others caught up, seized his bridle, and remonstrated.

literal: The emperor sighed deeply and said: "I am honored as Son of Heaven yet cannot be free!
idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "I am honored as Son of Heaven yet I am not free!

literal: " Gao Jiong said: "Your Majesty — how can you lightly regard all under Heaven for one woman?
idiomatic: " Gao Jiong said, "Your Majesty — how can you slight the empire for one woman?

literal: " The emperor's intent slightly eased; he halted his horse a long while; only at night did he return to the palace.
idiomatic: " The emperor's anger eased somewhat; he halted a long while and returned to the palace only at night.

literal: The empress waited for the emperor inside the gate; when the emperor arrived she wept and bowed in apology.
idiomatic: The empress waited inside the gate; when he arrived she wept and bowed in apology.

literal: Jiong, Su, and others reconciled them; the emperor set out wine and was extremely merry.
idiomatic: Jiong, Su, and the others mediated; the emperor set out wine and they were merry again.

literal: From this the empress's intent was quite broken.
idiomatic: From that time her jealousy was somewhat curbed.

literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Renshou, on the day jiazi, the sun had halos in four rings.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Renshou, on the day jiazi, the sun showed halos in four rings.

literal: On the day jisi.
idiomatic: On the day jisi.

literal: Great White invaded the Bushel.
idiomatic: The planet Venus crossed the Bushel constellation.

literal: That night the empress died in Yong'an Palace, age fifty-nine; she was buried at Tailing.
idiomatic: That night the empress died in Yong'an Palace, aged fifty-nine, and was buried at Tailing.

literal: Afterward Lady Xuanhua Chen and Lady Ronghua Cai both had favor; the emperor was quite infatuated — because of this illness arose.
idiomatic: Afterward Lady Xuanhua Chen and Lady Ronghua Cai both won favor; the emperor was deeply infatuated — illness followed.

literal: At the approach of death he told attendants: "Had the empress been here, I would not have come to this," he said.
idiomatic: As death approached he told his attendants, "Had the empress still been alive, I would not have come to this."

literal: Lady Xuanhua Chen was the daughter of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
idiomatic: Lady Xuanhua Chen was the daughter of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

literal: Her nature was intelligent and clever; in looks none could pair with her.
idiomatic: She was intelligent and without rival in beauty.

literal: When Chen perished she was assigned to the palace women; later she was chosen into the palace as consort.
idiomatic: When Chen fell she was assigned to the palace women; later she was chosen as a consort.

literal: At that time Empress Dugu was jealous; within the rear palace few could approach the emperor — only Chen had favor.
idiomatic: At that time Empress Dugu was fiercely jealous; few women in the rear palace could approach the emperor — only Lady Chen had favor.

literal: When Emperor Yang was in his princedom he secretly had a plan to seize the succession and schemed for inner support; he often sent gifts.
idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was still a prince he secretly plotted to seize the succession and sought allies within the palace, sending gifts often.

literal: He presented golden snakes, golden camels, and other objects to win Chen's favor.
idiomatic: He presented golden snakes, golden camels, and other curios to win her favor.

literal: At the time of the crown prince's deposition and establishment he had considerable force.
idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed and another installed, she had considerable influence.

literal: When Empress Dugu the Literary died she was advanced to noble lady.
idiomatic: After Empress Dugu died she was promoted to noble lady.

literal: She monopolized the chambers and favor; she decided inner affairs — within the six palaces none could compare.
idiomatic: She held exclusive favor and controlled inner affairs — none in the six palaces could compare.

literal: When the emperor approached death the testamentary edict invested her as Lady Xuanhua.
idiomatic: When the emperor was dying his final edict invested her as Lady Xuanhua.

literal: Earlier the emperor was ill at Renshou Palace; the lady and the crown prince together attended his illness.
idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Lady Chen and the crown prince attended him together.

literal: At dawn when changing clothes the crown prince forced her; the lady resisted and escaped.
idiomatic: At dawn, while she was changing clothes, the crown prince forced himself on her; she resisted and escaped.

literal: She returned to the emperor's side; the emperor wondered at her changed expression and asked.
idiomatic: She returned to the emperor's bedside; he noticed her altered expression and asked what had happened.

literal: The lady wept and told the truth.
idiomatic: She wept and told him the truth.

literal: The emperor in rage said: "This beast — how can he be entrusted with great affairs; Dugu truly misled me!
idiomatic: The emperor raged, "That beast — how can he be entrusted with the realm! Dugu truly misled me!

literal: " He meant the Literary Empress.
idiomatic: " He meant Empress Dugu.

literal: He then called Minister of War Liu Shu and Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Yan and said: "Summon my son!
idiomatic: He then called the Minister of War Liu Shu and the attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Yan and said, "Summon my son!

literal: " Shu and the rest called the crown prince.
idiomatic: " They called for the crown prince.

literal: The emperor said: "Yong.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yong.

literal: " Shu and Yan left the gate; when the edict document was finished they showed it to Left Pushe Yang Su.
idiomatic: " Shu and Yan left the gate; when the edict was drafted they showed it to the Left Pushe Yang Su.

literal: Su reported to the crown prince; the crown prince sent Zhang Heng into the sleeping hall and then ordered the lady and all in the rear palace attending illness to go to separate chambers.
idiomatic: Su informed the crown prince, who sent Zhang Heng into the sleeping hall and had Lady Chen and all the women attending the sick removed to other chambers.

literal: Soon they heard the emperor had died, yet mourning was not yet proclaimed.
idiomatic: Soon word came that the emperor had died, but the mourning had not yet been announced.

literal: The lady and the women of the rear palace looked at each other and said: "Affairs have changed!
idiomatic: Lady Chen and the palace women looked at one another and said, "Everything has changed!

literal: " All their colors moved and their legs trembled.
idiomatic: " Their faces went pale and their legs shook.

literal: In the afternoon the crown prince sent an envoy bearing a gold casket; paper was pasted on the seam; he personally wrote the seal character on the closure and bestowed it on the lady.
idiomatic: That afternoon the crown prince sent an envoy with a gold casket, sealed at the edge in his own hand, and gave it to Lady Chen.

literal: The lady saw it and was afraid, thinking it poison; she did not dare open it.
idiomatic: She was terrified, thinking it held poison, and dared not open it.

literal: The envoy urged her; only then did she open it and see within the casket several knotted cords of one heart.
idiomatic: The envoy pressed her; at last she opened it and found several lover's knots inside.

literal: The palace women said to each other: "We are spared death!
idiomatic: The palace women said to one another, "We are spared!

literal: " Chen in anger sat back and would not bow in thanks.
idiomatic: " Lady Chen, furious, sat back and refused to thank the envoy.

literal: The palace women together pressed her; only then did she bow to the envoy.
idiomatic: The other women pressed her until she bowed to the envoy.
